criteria.asks: Is there a machine-readable description of every HTTP door?
criteria.note: 112 paths described

criteria.asks: Can an agent find that description without being told where it is?
criteria.note: RFC 9727 catalog served at the well-known path

criteria.asks: Are the payment terms readable before anyone spends?
criteria.note: x402 discovery document served

criteria.asks: Does a free instrument answer a caller holding no key at all?
criteria.note: answered 400 to an anonymous, keyless call

criteria.asks: Does the description cover the paid doors, not just the free ones?
criteria.note: 27 documented 402 responses

criteria.asks: Does the MCP door answer tools/list over streamable HTTP?
criteria.how: curl -s -X POST https://scvd.store/mcp -H "content-type: application/json" -H "accept: application/json, text/event-stream" -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
criteria.note: 13 tools listed

criteria.asks: Does every tool declare whether it is read-only before it runs?
criteria.how: the same tools/list call; check each tool for annotations.readOnlyHint
criteria.note: all 13 tools annotated

criteria.asks: Is every tool described in prose a model can route on, with a typed input schema?
criteria.how: the same tools/list call; check description length and inputSchema
criteria.note: all 13 tools typed and described

criteria.asks: Can an agent buy without leaving MCP for a browser?
criteria.how: the same tools/list call; look for buy_* tools and their x402 terms
criteria.note: 6 buy tools, each naming its payment path

criteria.asks: Does the public registry repeat the description we currently publish?
criteria.how: compare server.json's description against the isLatest entry at https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=scvd
criteria.note: published 0.2.1 says "The trust layer of the x402 economy: free conformance checks, attestation, corpus, agent store." — server.json (0.2.2) says "Evidence observatory for agentic commerce: free x402 conformance checks, corpus, agent store."

criteria.asks: Is the content in the served HTML, or does it need a client to build it?
criteria.note: content server-rendered; 2 executable script tag(s) on the page

criteria.asks: Is one look at the front door cheap?
criteria.note: 101 KB, budget 195 KB

criteria.asks: Does a pixel-reading agent get told there is a text road it could take instead?
criteria.note: robots.txt names the text maps; llms.txt answers

criteria.asks: Does an unremarkable client get the page, or a challenge?
criteria.note: plain fetch, no challenge, robots allows

criteria.asks: Can a generic tool find the content by structure alone?
criteria.note: landmarks present: <main <h1 <section

criteria.asks: Is there anything on the page a script can hold that is not a style class?
criteria.note: no first-party data-* attributes and no ids: every hook is a style class, which redesigns move

criteria.asks: Is getting around the site real hrefs rather than script handlers?
criteria.note: 42 plain links; navigation needs no script

criteria.asks: Does each page point at its own machine-readable twin, so nobody has to scrape it?
criteria.note: alternate representation linked from the page head

criteria.asks: Is there a browser-door script at all?
criteria.note: registerTool declarations served

criteria.asks: Are the browser's tool names the same objects the MCP door serves, or a second hand-typed list?
criteria.how: compare the names in /webmcp.js against the names in the MCP tools/list answer
criteria.note: 5 browser tools, every one a read-only tool the MCP door also serves

criteria.asks: Do the rooms an agent lands in declare the door, or only the front page?
criteria.how: fetch every URL in /sitemap.xml and grep for the /webmcp.js script tag
criteria.note: 28 of 68 published rooms declare it (41%)

criteria.asks: Will a shipping Chrome still enable the API on our origin tomorrow?
criteria.how: read the origin-trial meta on https://scvd.store/ and base64-decode its payload
criteria.note: origin trial valid until 2026-11-17 (79 days)

criteria.asks: Is the zero-JavaScript path — toolname on a form — taken anywhere in the store?
criteria.how: fetch every URL in /sitemap.xml as a browser and grep for '<form ... toolname='
criteria.note: no annotated form in any published room — the cheapest declaration in the lineup is untaken

criteria.asks: Does the store put its own model between a visitor and the shelf?
criteria.note: no chat box; the visiting agent is the visitor

criteria.asks: Is the thing a chat box would have explained published as text any model can read?
criteria.note: llms.txt (19 KB) and /agents.md carry the guide

criteria.asks: Can any model use the doors, or does one host have to be in the loop?
criteria.how: the MCP tools/list answer: JSON Schema inputs, no host-specific fields
criteria.note: all 13 tools typed in plain JSON Schema
